To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a nonimmunized phage library allowed the isolation of three neutralizing human scFvs against crotoxin, which are specific for the same region of one sub‐unit of this toxin.
we have obtained three scFvs from a human phage library that recognize crotoxin.
the use of combinatorial phage display technology to make human antibodies against crotoxin is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of human scFvs against the main toxic component (crotoxin) of the South American rattlesnake venom.
the development of a new strategy for passive immunization against the effects of snake venom.
the development of new therapeutic strategies to treat envenomation by the venom of South‐American rattlers, a serious public health problem in Brazil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human scFvs are able to neutralize the biological activity of crotoxin, and therefore may be a good alternative for the treatment of Crotalus bites.
the scFvs 1 and 8 are capable of neutralizing crotoxin in vitro, and scFv8 also neutralizes crotoxin in vivo.
this study is an example of how to use phage display technology to make human anticrotoxins scFvs with in vivo neutralising activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated from a human phage display library scFvs that neutralized the toxicity of crotoxin, a component of the venom from a South American rattlesnake.
human antibodies can be isolated from nonimmunized individuals and can be used to neutralize toxins in vivo and in vitro.
the use of a combinatorial phage library allowed the isolation of human scFvs which are capable to recognize crotoxin, to neutralize its lethal effects and to reduce its myotoxic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of phage display technology allows the isolation of neutralizing human antibodies against crotoxin, a toxin from snake venom.
it is possible to isolate human antitoxins from a naïve library of scFv clones.
it is possible to obtain neutralizing scFvs from a nonimmunized human library.
